resolution: Built the transform gizmo (move + resize) — the last first-slice Studio piece. Pure ops in editMesh.ts: vertsCentroid/vertsHalfExtent/translateVerts/scaleVerts (3 new tests; editMesh now 15/15). New meshGizmo.tsx holds the 2D overlay (TransformGizmo: RGB arrows for move, square handles + center hub for resize), the handle hit-test (pickGizmoHandle), selection->verts gather (selectionVertIndices), and the screen-drag->world mapping (axisScreen/dragWorldDistance, frozen at mouse-down so perspective at the anchor is honored). The gizmo anchors on the selection's best center (the vertex itself / edge midpoint / face center / centroid of a multi-select) and is drawn through the meshSelect projector as the viewport's last 2D children, so the arrows are NEVER occluded by geometry (USER hard rule). Studio.tsx viewport: a move|resize toggle joins the element toolbar; onDown checks the gizmo before pick/orbit; a drag mutates a viewport-local draft (re-lowered live, only the dragged part) and commits to the store on mouse-up, running the concave Auto-Fix guard (splitConcaveFaces) on commit — commit-on-release, no per-move store write that would melt the frame. Two store changes made it correct: per-part lift is now FROZEN at mint (editing verts no longer slides the part to re-seat on the grid), and a meshRev counter re-lowers committed geometry without refitting the camera (separate from revision). Auto-Fix auto-splits (the recommended action); the Revert/Ignore dialog is a later refinement. All four TSX files bundle clean; user confirmed it looks good in-app. Hot-reload TSX, nothing committed.
